clue.text: Draw article without decoration as a guide

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside or beyond, so the decoration stands on the outside before the article

parts.note: to drag is to draw or pull along
OM is the Order of Merit, a British decoration
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is told to sketch a plain, unadorned item to serve as a model.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is read in its old sense of 'outside', so the decoration stands outside, ahead of the article. 'Draw' looks like the instruction to sketch, and 'decoration' like ornament; it is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragoman is an interpreter and guide in Arabic-, Turkish- or Persian-speaking countries.

clue.text: Beastly manoeuvring becomes habit over a period

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places the first piece above the second

parts.note: a habit is a garment, such as a nun's or a riding outfit, so dress
an age is a long span of time

explanation.surface: Bad behaviour, over time, hardens into routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' suggests nastiness, but means done by a beast: a horse performing set movements.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the training of a horse to perform precise movements at its rider's commands.

clue.text: One is glad maybe to be nearby

annotationWithheld.why: One is glad maybe to be nearby (9) as held: no parse of 'One is glad maybe' giving ALONGSIDE found; the definition is 'to be nearby' but the wordplay could not be identified

clue.text: Doctor upset, say, over a long letter

indicators.note: in a down answer, over places these pieces above the final letter
upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the doctor's letters run backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, an army doctor
eg, for example, is what say means here

explanation.surface: A distressed physician comments on a lengthy piece of correspondence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long letter' looks like a lengthy epistle, but omega is the Greek letter for a long o.
explanation.definitionFit: Omega is the Greek long o, as opposed to omicron, the short o.

clue.text: Athlete's opening 11 on the beach

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

parts.note: 11 refers to the answer to 11 across, a justification, which is a ground for something

explanation.surface: A runner's first ground is the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: Clue 11 across answers RATIONALE; a ground is a reason.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship run aground is stranded on the shore or shallows, as if beached.

clue.text: Gives the letters of magic formulae

explanation.surface: Someone spells out the words of a set of incantations.
explanation.definitionFit: To spell a word is to give its letters in order; spells are also charms or incantations used in magic.

clue.text: Careful and quiet — driven to take a break

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone who is cautious and reserved feels compelled to go on holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: Provident means prudent in providing for the future, thrifty and far-sighted.

clue.text: The sovereign owns a place in the mountains

parts.note: a sovereign is a one-pound coin, and L is the symbol for a pound
to own is to have, so has

explanation.surface: A monarch possesses a mountain retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The sovereign' suggests a monarch, but it is the gold coin worth a pound, L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lhasa is the capital of Tibet, high in the Himalayas.

clue.text: Cultivated Europeans

parts.note: seemingly refined Scandinavians, but read as grown crops sharing a national name

explanation.definitionFit: Swedes are root vegetables grown as crops, and also people from Sweden.

clue.text: Emphasize need for a second lock

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for a second of time
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: Someone insists on the need for an extra lock on the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock' suggests a door fitting, but it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress something is to put weight or importance on it.

clue.text: Call up the first lady to receive approval

indicators.note: the first lady takes in the approval, which sits inside her name

parts.note: Eve, in the Bible the first woman
OK is a word of approval or assent

explanation.surface: A request to phone the President's wife so she can give the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first lady' suggests a president's wife, but it is Eve from Genesis, holding OK.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke something is to summon or bring it to mind, as a memory is summoned.

clue.text: Set a limit on the drink with good reason

parts.note: to ration a thing is to restrict how much of it each person may have
ale is beer, a common drink

explanation.surface: A publican justifies limiting how much customers may drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A rationale is the underlying logic or justification behind a course of action.

clue.text: A name made by writing.

parts.note: read plainly, a personal mark written by hand at the foot of a letter or cheque

explanation.definitionFit: Your handwritten autograph on a document is your own name written out in ink.

clue.text: Popular with an Oriental? Ridiculous!

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
taken as written
E stands for East, so for something Oriental

explanation.surface: An exclamation dismissing the idea that being popular with Easterners matters.
explanation.definitionFit: Inane means silly or senseless, lacking sense, which is what something ridiculous is.

clue.text: Possibly diverge when upset

indicators.note: possibly signals that the letters of the next word might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: People might part ways when they are angry with each other.
explanation.definitionFit: To be grieved is to be distressed or hurt, the feeling of someone upset by a loss.

clue.text: Substituted for another one caught — captured by divers

indicators.note: the first pieces are held inside the word that follows

parts.note: divers is an old word for several or various
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: A replacement person is caught and then seized by underwater swimmers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divers' is not underwater swimmers but the old adjective meaning several.
explanation.definitionFit: Vicarious means experienced or acting in place of someone else, as a deputy does.

clue.text: Sound footwork, that's plain

indicators.note: sound here means said aloud, so what follows is a word heard rather than seen

parts.note: a step is a single movement of the feet, as in dancing

explanation.surface: Praise for a dancer's solid footwork, described as simple and unfussy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid, but it is the homophone signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The steppe is a vast treeless grassland, a plain of the kind found across Russia and Central Asia.

clue.text: "Tramping", a new game

indicators.note: new signals that the preceding letters are made into a fresh word

explanation.surface: Hiking is described as a novel sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' looks like a pastime, but means wild birds hunted for sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The ptarmigan is a grouse of mountain and Arctic regions, shot as game.

clue.text: Colours, and that's normal

explanation.surface: Flags flying, and everything is as usual.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a regimental flag, also called its colours; standard also means usual or typical.

clue.text: The dealer's a little schemer — certain to cheat

indicators.note: only a little of the words that follow is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A trader is portrayed as a small-time plotter sure to cheat customers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'scheMER CERtain'; 'to cheat' completes the surface only.
explanation.definitionFit: A mercer is a trader in textiles, especially fine silks and velvets.

clue.text: A log — note amount of wood in it

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a cord is a measure of cut firewood

explanation.surface: A single log, with a memo stating how much timber it contains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Log' suggests timber, matching the wood, but means a written register.
explanation.definitionFit: A record is a written account of events, like a ship's logbook.

clue.text: Draw for use, of spare court

parts.note: extra means additional or spare

explanation.surface: A lottery-style draw held to allocate an unused tennis court.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to pull or draw something out, as a dentist removes a tooth.

clue.text: Sort of band capable of adapting to change

explanation.surface: A musical group described as flexible.
explanation.definitionFit: An elastic band is a rubber loop; elastic also means flexible or adaptable.

clue.text: Lays up gold, which causes amazement

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down, so puts
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Someone stockpiles gold, and everyone is astonished.
explanation.definitionFit: Stupor is a dazed state of stunned bewilderment, as when astonished.

clue.text: Fall off, causing a spill

explanation.surface: Someone takes a tumble off a bike or horse.
explanation.definitionFit: To taper is to dwindle or diminish gradually; a taper is also a thin strip of wood or wax for lighting fires, also known as a spill.

clue.text: An American writing poetry for money

explanation.surface: A US poet working for cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezra Pound was an American poet; the pound is also British currency.

clue.text: Warn macho eccentric to get cleaner

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters before it are to be scrambled

explanation.surface: A warning to an odd tough guy to tidy himself up.
explanation.definitionFit: A charwoman is a woman paid to clean houses or offices.

clue.text: Offal can be used to make a stew

indicators.note: the letters given can be rearranged to form the answer

explanation.surface: Advice that animal innards are good for a casserole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offal' looks like animal innards for the pot, but means rubbish or refuse.
explanation.definitionFit: Offal in its older sense means refuse or scraps, rubbish thrown away.

clue.text: Rich man is just the same as an underworld boss at grabbing credit

indicators.note: the god and the word at together seize the credit and hold it between them

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god ruling the realm of the dead
taken as written
CR is the abbreviation for credit in accounts

explanation.surface: A wealthy financier is likened to a gangster for seizing loans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Underworld boss' points to a mobster, but it is the Roman god of the dead; 'grabbing' has the god's name and 'at' clasp the credit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A plutocrat is a person whose power derives from wealth.

clue.text: A thousand warriors backed this Greek character

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the whole sequence before it is read in reverse

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand
GIs are American soldiers

explanation.surface: A large army supported a particular Greek hero.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, a character in that script.

clue.text: Salad food for an artist?

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts
a dish is a prepared item of food

explanation.surface: A question about what to serve a painter for lunch.
explanation.definitionFit: A radish is a crunchy red root eaten raw as a salad vegetable.

clue.text: Shown on TV as guarded

explanation.surface: A programme broadcast under heavy protection.
explanation.definitionFit: A film screened is broadcast or shown; to be screened is also to be shielded or protected from view.
